title: Atlas Q2 orchestration & staffing plan for hosted API + model catalog
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Produce a tightly scoped quarterly orchestration and staffing plan that lets the Hosted API team introduce a phased model-catalog rotation for Q2 with predictable latency and capacity headroom. We will define cohort sizes, canary windows, staffing on-call rotations, and gating criteria tied to model quality signals and infra SLOs. This ticket coordinates PM, Eng, and DevEx workstreams and produces a single-page operational runbook plus a staffing roster and a set of gating dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Operational runbook (one-pager) published in Confluence with rollback/playbook steps
Canary schedule defined with cohort sizes and traffic split for 3 staging cohorts
Staffing rota published with primary/secondary hours for canary windows and 1 escalation lead
Dashboards created in MetriX showing token-level latency, batch size distribution, and cache hit rate
Gating rules codified: latency increase >15% or error rate >1% triggers automatic rollback
Dependencies on ENG (autoscaler, kernel pinning) validated with smoke test on staging
comments: 2026-01-12 | Maya Chen: Draft plan created after sync with Eng infra and Runtime teams. Initial ask: define 3 canary cohorts (1%, 5%, 20%) and a single rollback threshold. Linking draft runbook.

2026-01-19 | Liam O'Connor: Eng feasibility review - autoscaler warmup time is 8 minutes for Dedicated pools; recommended extending canary windows to 30m to measure steady-state QPS and KV cache warming.
2026-01-22 | Priya Rao (SRE): Added suggestion to monitor batch size distribution and introduce a batch-saturation alert; shared a proof-of-concept PromQL query.

2026-01-28 | Maya Chen: Incorporated SRE feedback. Trade-off noted: longer windows increase exposure but reduce false positives from transient warmups. Added explicit escalation path and on-call assignments.
2026-02-04 | DevEx (Ana Gutierrez): Suggested a lightweight CLI tool to seed cohorts in staging and capture prompt-set evaluation results; allocated 2 points from DevEx sprint.
2026-02-10 | Liam O'Connor: Trial run scheduled on staging for 2026-02-17. Dependency ENG-5420 (kernel selection flag) must land before the trial. PR referenced.

2026-02-18 | Maya Chen: Trial completed on staging; observed 9% token-latency increase at 20% cohort when cache miss rate rose >6%. Decided to add a soft throttle at 20% traffic to let KV cache stabilize; follow-up ENG task opened.
decisions: Adopt 3-cohort progression: seed (1%), ramp (5%), broad canary (20%)
Extend canary windows to 30 minutes per cohort to account for autoscaler and KV cache warmup
Soft throttle at broad canary level if cache-miss rate >5% to avoid transient latency spikes
Tie rollback to composite metric: (error_rate > 1%) OR (latency_p90 increase > 15% AND cache_miss_rate > 4%)
tradeoffs: Longer canary windows reduce false positives but increase exposure window for problematic models
Soft throttling protects SLOs at cost of slower rollout velocity and slightly higher user-facing variability during ramp
Allocating senior Eng on-call during canaries increases cost but materially reduces time-to-rollback
risk_mitigation: Pre-rollout smoke tests run against a mirrored traffic fixture to validate kernel selection and quantization behavior
Customer cohort opt-in flag for early access customers to limit blast radius
Runbook includes manual and automated rollback steps and postmortem template

SRE to add batch-saturation alert and dashboard tile - due 2026-02-24

notes_for_execs: Goal: reduce model-lineup-induced latency regressions during quarterly rotations by making canaries predictable and staffed. Expected outcome: 30% reduction in production incidents attributable to model swaps vs last quarter. We will report topline signal after first two pilots.
implementation_notes: Prefer non-breaking config flags to route by policy (region/tier) so rollouts can be scoped without infra deploys
KV cache priming recommended using historical prefix replay for 15 minutes prior to ramping to 20%
Use 'fallback-to-variant' policy to degrade to smaller quantized model only if composite rollback triggers
